name: osc-bridge
description: OSC ↔ MIDI/SysEx bridge for synths and DAWs, with the SynthHub catalogue — a MIDI MCP and OSC MCP.
long_description: osc-bridge is a declarative bridge between OSC and the music world: hardware synthesizers over MIDI/SysEx, plus music software over OSC (Ableton, Bitwig, Reaper, Sonic Pi, SuperCollider, Pure Data, TouchDesigner, VCV Rack). Its MCP server exposes the SynthHub catalogue of drivers to an LLM, fetching each driver when needed — list devices, read a device's named OSC surface, send OSC to synths and DAWs, and check a running bridge's status. Both a MIDI MCP (hardware over MIDI/SysEx) and an OSC MCP (DAWs and live-coding environments).

default_target.title: Default OSC target
default_target.description: host:port that the send / get_status tools use when no target argument is given. Defaults to 127.0.0.1:7777 — the standard `osc-bridge run` bind.

tools.name: list_devices
tools.description: Find device drivers in the catalogue of synths, drum machines, controllers and DAWs. Without arguments it lists them all; `query` keeps drivers whose vendor, name or slug contain every word (e.g. 'korg minilogue'). Returns name, vendor, OSC prefix (slug), kind, source tier and firmware version when the source states one. Pass the slug to list_routes for the full CC/NRPN/SysEx map.

limit.description: Return at most this many drivers.

query.description: Words that must all appear in the vendor, name or slug (case-insensitive).

tools.name: get_device_docs
tools.description: Fetch the markdown companion documentation for one device, if present. The slug is the device's OSC prefix without the leading slash (e.g. 'ableton' for /ableton).

tools.name: list_routes
tools.description: Return the OSC routes a device exposes: declarative commands (OSC paths it accepts), cc/nrpn params, sysex params, named note triggers (drum sounds), and reply patterns. Use this to discover what a device can do.

tools.name: export_device
tools.description: Write one driver in a format other tools read, any of the formats of osd-formats: 'oscquery' gives its OSC namespace as OSCQuery JSON (every route with type tags, ranges and access, for OSC controllers and browsers); 'midnam' gives its MIDI names as a MIDI Name Document (controllers incl. NRPN/RPN, named values, drum notes per channel, for DAWs such as Ardour or Logic); 'deluge' gives the definition file of a Deluge; and the others in the enum. Each carries the credit and licence of the driver's sources. The document is the text content; an OSCQuery namespace is large (every address, each CC 0-127 included). It only reads: to put an export on a device, use install_export.

device.description: Driver id (e.g. 'korg/minilogue') or slug, from list_devices.

tools.name: install_export
tools.description: Put the export of one driver (device) on another device plugged into this computer (on), in one gesture the same for every target: the format the target receives, the path of the file and the way it is sent (a file written by SysEx, step by step) all come from the target's own driver, and a target that declares nothing it receives is refused. This may OVERWRITE a file on the device (it is not read first): without confirm_overwrite: true nothing is sent, and the call returns what it would write (format, way, path, size, what the format could not carry); confirm with the user, then call again with confirm_overwrite: true. A target that is not plugged in is refused before any message; a send that fails on the way says the step reached and the messages already sent, with no retry and no undo.

confirm_overwrite.description: True once the user agreed that the file may be overwritten on the target; without it nothing is sent.

device.description: The driver to export: id (e.g. 'korg/minilogue') or slug, from list_devices.

on.description: The device that receives it: its catalogue id or slug; its driver says what it receives.

tools.name: list_roles
tools.description: List the roles of a driver's controls (OSD paths such as filter/cutoff), most important first, each with its address, range, default and steps. A driver without roles gives an empty list.

limit.description: Keep only the first roles, up to this number.

tools.name: set_by_role
tools.description: Set a control by its role (e.g. filter/cutoff) without knowing its address or numbers. value is from 0 to 1 on the range of the role; osc-bridge scales it on the range and steps of this driver. Sent like `send`. A role whose control writes the device's memory is refused: restore_presets (confirm_overwrite) does that.

role.description: The role as listed by list_roles, e.g. filter/cutoff.

target.description: Optional override host:port. Defaults to MCP server's --default-target.

value.description: From 0 to 1 on the range of the role.

tools.name: get_by_role
tools.description: Read a control's current value by its role: sends the read request the driver declares and gives the reply's value from 0 to 1 on the range of the role. A driver that declares no read for the control says it does not report it.

role.description: The role as listed by list_roles.

target.description: Optional override host:port. Defaults to MCP server's --default-target.

tools.name: send
tools.description: Send a single OSC message to a running osc-bridge instance. Target defaults to the server's --default-target. Args are typed (int, float, string, bool).

args.description: Typed args. Each item is one of {int}, {float}, {string}, {bool}.

target.description: Optional override host:port (e.g. 127.0.0.1:7777). Defaults to MCP server's --default-target.

tools.name: get_status
tools.description: Send /bridge/status to a running osc-bridge and wait briefly for one reply per device (up to 500 ms).

tools.name: add_link
tools.description: Link two addresses of a running orchestrator, live: the next message at `from` also goes to `to`, with no restart. Optionally scale the first argument from an input range to an output range. Refused, with an error that names the address or the chain, when a device or an address is unknown to its driver, or when the chain of links would loop or pass four hops; nothing changes then.

target.description: host:port of the orchestrator, defaults to --default-target

tools.name: remove_link
tools.description: Remove a link of a running orchestrator, live: the next message no longer follows it. Refused, naming the link, when it does not exist.

target.description: host:port of the orchestrator, defaults to --default-target

tools.name: list_links
tools.description: List the links of a running orchestrator, those of its configuration file and those added live: one reply per link with its source, its target, its origin ('file' or 'live') and its scaling, then a final count.

target.description: host:port of the orchestrator, defaults to --default-target

tools.name: backup_presets
tools.description: Back up a hardware device's presets as a .syx file. The device is named (device: a catalogue id or slug, see list_devices): its driver says which messages are its sounds, on any channel or device number, and how to ask for them. Listens on the device's MIDI input and records those messages (a 'bulk dump'), stopping 3 s after the last one. Either the user starts the dump from the device's menu during the call, or pass out_port and the driver's dump request is sent. Use detect_hardware first to find the ports.

device.description: The device's catalogue id or slug (e.g. 'korg/minilogue'); a device the catalogue does not know has to be described first.

file.description: Path of the .syx file to write.

in_port.description: MIDI IN port of the device: index or name fragment (e.g. 'minilab').

out_port.description: MIDI OUT port: the driver's dump request is sent on it first (index or name fragment).

tools.name: restore_presets
tools.description: Send a .syx file to a hardware device, e.g. to restore a preset backup. This OVERWRITES the device's memory: confirm with the user first, then pass confirm_overwrite: true. The device is named (device): its driver sets the pause between messages, refuses a bank that cannot be written before anything is sent, and the sounds are sent on the configured channel. For a sound that carries no place, pass bank and number.

bank.description: The bank to write into, by name or place (with number), for a sound that carries no place.

confirm_overwrite.description: Must be true: the user agreed to overwrite the device's memory.

device.description: The device's catalogue id or slug (e.g. 'korg/minilogue'); a device the catalogue does not know has to be described first.

file.description: Path of the .syx file to send.

number.description: The program number to write into, as the device shows it (with bank).

out_port.description: MIDI OUT port of the device: index or name fragment.

tools.name: detect_hardware
tools.description: Find the MIDI devices plugged into this computer and match them to catalogue drivers. Lists MIDI ports, sends the standard MIDI Identity Request, then the makers' own identity requests the drivers name (harmless: they change nothing on the device), and reads each device's manufacturer, model and firmware. A driver whose identity block recognises the reply (or the USB port name) comes first, the variant for the firmware read from it above the others; of drivers matching equally, the one the others share their MIDI with comes first, and each lists the others in equally_matching. Returns, per device, the best matching drivers (with recognised_by and firmware when recognised) and a ready-to-run 'osc-bridge run' command with the right port numbers.

probe.description: Send the Identity Request (default true). False only lists ports and matches by port name.

timeout_ms.description: How long to wait for identity replies, 100-5000 ms (default 800).
